PullRequest.Title: Layout: apply an arrangement of the side bars and the panel at once
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

This adds a way to apply an arrangement of the primary side bar, the panel and the secondary side bar at once. It is the groundwork for named layouts (#348819), which let a window switch between saved arrangements. Nothing calls the new methods yet, so apart from the two changes to existing code at the end this changes no behavior. The named layouts code that will call them comes in a later PR, behind `workbench.namedLayouts.enabled`.

## Why

The existing layout methods are made for user actions, not for going to a stored arrangement:

- Showing a part opens its last view container, and showing the panel focuses it.
- Hiding a part moves the focus to the panel or the editor.
- Maximizing the secondary side bar hides and shows the other parts one after the other.
- Moving the panel shows it first.
- Part sizes are only read from storage when the window starts.

Switching layouts by calling these one after the other passes through intermediate arrangements, each with its side effects. The first named layouts implementation did that: a focused terminal brought back a panel that had just been hidden, view containers opened (and activated their extensions) only to be replaced, and sizes drifted.

## What changes

- `IPartsLayoutState` in `layoutService.ts`: visibility and size of the side bars and the panel, the panel position, and whether the panel or the secondary side bar is maximized.
- `Layout.getPartsLayoutState()` returns it. While the secondary side bar is maximized, it describes the other parts as they show when it is restored.
- `Layout.applyPartsLayoutState()` writes the state into the layout's state model and creates the grid from it, the same way the window does at startup, replacing the old grid. Disposing a grid does not dispose its parts. Specifics of applying:
  - It applies only once the workbench layout is created. The window creates its grid from the arrangement that it restores from workspace storage, so the method doesn't handle the time before that. Called earlier, it reports an unexpected error and changes nothing. The method is new in this PR and nothing calls it yet; the named layouts code that will call it can wait for the layout.
  - It does not move the focus to another part: the element that had the focus gets it back while its part shows, and otherwise the focus goes where `focus()` puts it. When that is a maximized part whose view container opens only later, the focus goes there as it opens, unless something else has the focus by then. Content that a part shows outside its element, as an editor does for a notebook or a webview, counts as in that part, as for `hasFocus()`.
  - It tells the parts whose visibility changed, as showing or hiding them in a grid does, so that context keys such as the one for Restore Panel stay correct.
  - It opens the last active view container of a part that shows, without focus, and closes the active one of a part that hides. An open that waits for the extensions to register is dropped when another state applies meanwhile, or when its part hides or gets a view container, since opening it would show the part again. For this, `openViewContainer()` takes an optional check; its existing callers behave as before. When the view container that was active last in the panel or the secondary side bar has no views yet, as an extension's has none until the extensions register, it waits for the extensions to register and chooses then, rather than showing another view container or none as showing the part by hand does.
  - It hides a visible chat part for a maximized panel or secondary side bar, as maximizing them does, and shows it again when they are restored. A maximized secondary side bar is created directly, as when the window starts with it; this relies on the change to `setAuxiliaryBarMaximized()` below.
  - It keeps an editor area that is hidden for the chat part hidden, and a banner that shows visible.
  - It fires the panel position and secondary side bar maximized events.
- Grid creation moves into `createWorkbenchGrid()`, which startup and applying share. The `startupLayout` telemetry event moves out of `createGridDescriptor()` into `logStartupLayout()`, so it is still sent once at startup, with the same values.
- The methods are only on `Layout` for now. They will be added to `IWorkbenchLayoutService` with the PR that uses them.

## Fix: width of the editor area with the panel on the left or right

When the grid is created, `arrangeMiddleSectionNodes()` subtracted the panel's width from the editor area only when no panel size was stored, which is almost never the case. While the editor area shows, the grid corrects this when it lays out. A hidden editor area, as for a maximized panel, keeps the width that is too large, and restoring the panel then takes the room from the side bars. The panel is now subtracted unless it is hidden. This also affects a window that starts with a maximized panel on the left or right. I verified the fix by applying a state, not by reloading a window.

The same holds for a maximized panel on the left or right under a maximized secondary side bar, which keeps the editor area hidden until the panel is restored too. The editor area then shows after the other parts, at its width from creating the grid, which counted the side bar and the panel that the maximize hid as 0, so it took their room back from the side bars. Creating the grid now gives the editor area in that case the width that the side bar, the chat part, the panel and the secondary side bar leave it once they show again at their sizes from before maximizing. A window that starts with this arrangement creates the same grid; a test with the sizes saved as on shutdown checks that it still gives the parts their widths back, also beside the chat part.

## Change: the chat part keeps its own width while it is hidden by a maximized secondary side bar, or has the editor area

`setAuxiliaryBarMaximized()` hid the side bar and the panel while the chat part still showed, and then the chat part. Since #349423, a part that hides beside the chat part gives its width to the chat part, so the width remembered for the hidden chat part included theirs (400 + 250 = 650), and restoring gave it back as they showed again. That only works when the same parts show again at the same sizes, which isn't the case when a layout is applied while the secondary side bar is maximized.

Beside a visible editor area, maximizing now hides the chat part before the side bar and the panel, and restoring shows it after them, so the chat part remembers its own width, also in its stored layout. With the editor area hidden for the chat part, the order is unchanged. A window that is maximized as it updates has stored the larger width, and shows the chat part once at that width after restoring.

As the chat part now shows after the other parts, while the secondary side bar still takes most of the room, the room that it needs came from the side bar and a panel on the left or right. After a reload while maximized, restoring left the side bar at its minimum width (found in Code OSS, see below). When the chat part shows again, the side bar and a panel on the left or right now get back the width they had before maximizing, once the secondary side bar has its own width again.

To check that maximizing and restoring isn't otherwise affected, I compared the part sizes before maximizing, while maximized and after restoring, with the old and the new order, in 216 arrangements in the unit test harness: side bar left or right; panel at the bottom, left or right; panel aligned center, justified or left; the chat part anchored to the side bar, the secondary side bar or the panel; each with the panel shown, the panel hidden, the editor area hidden for the chat part, and a reload while maximized. 213 are the same. The other 3 are a reload while maximized with the panel on the right, where the chat part now comes back at its width from before maximizing (380), not at 328. That harness's reload didn't restore the saved sizes of the parts, which is why it missed the side bar's width above; a test now saves them as the layout does as the window closes.

While the editor area is hidden for the chat part, the chat part fills the editor area's width too, and `saveChatPartLayout()` stored that width. A grid created from it, as a window reloads or a state applies, gave the hidden editor area the width that was left, none, so the editor area showed again at its minimum width and the chat part kept the rest. While it has the editor area, the chat part now stores its own width: its width less the width that the hidden editor area shows again at. This also fixes the reload, which on `main` loses the editor area's width the same way.

## How to test

New tests in `src/vs/workbench/test/browser/layout.test.ts`, suite "parts layout state". Each fails without the part of the change it covers:

- Applying an arrangement gives the same grid as starting the window with it, does not move the focus, and only tells the side bar that it hid.
- A maximized secondary side bar, and restoring it.
- A maximized panel, and restoring it.
- Restoring a maximized panel on the right takes its room back from the panel, not from the side bars (the fix above).
- An editor area hidden for the chat part is not described as a maximized panel, and stays hidden when an applied maximized secondary side bar is restored.
- A maximized panel or secondary side bar that is applied hides the chat part, which keeps its width as states apply and shows again at it when they are restored.
- The element that had the focus keeps it while its part shows, and the focus goes to the editor when its part hides.
- Content that an editor shows outside its element has the focus in the editor, which goes to the maximized part when the editor area hides.
- A banner that shows keeps showing.
- A state that applies before the grid exists changes nothing, and reports an error.
- A view container that opens once the extensions register does not show its part when another state hid it meanwhile, and still opens when its part stays shown.
- A panel whose view container that was active last is an extension's shows it once the extensions register, rather than another or none.
- The focus that goes to a maximized secondary side bar, as the editor area that had it hides, goes to the view container that opens there once the extensions register, unless something has the focus by then.
- A chat part that has the editor area keeps its own width, so that the editor area shows again at its width after a state applies or the window reloads (the change above).
- A maximized panel that applies while the chat part has the editor area restores the widths, as maximizing it does.
- Restoring the secondary side bar, maximized beside the chat part as the window reloaded, gives the parts their widths from before (the change above).
- A state applies as from a window without a maximized part, also while the secondary side bar is maximized beside the chat part: a wider side bar, a hidden side bar, and a maximized panel on the right.
- Maximizing the secondary side bar hides the chat part at its own width, not with the width of the parts it hides beside it, also across a reload (the change above).
- A secondary side bar maximized over a maximized panel, restored and then the panel, gives the parts their widths from before, with the panel at the bottom, left and right (the fix above).
- A window that starts with the secondary side bar maximized over a maximized panel on the left or right gives the parts their widths from before, also beside the chat part.

The test harness's activity bar now has a fixed width, as the real one does. Without it, the activity bar took up width that the chat part lost.

Validation, on Windows, on the latest commit of this PR:

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `node build/oxlint.ts` on the changed files: passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/layout.test.ts`: 71 passing
- `.\scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/test/browser/parts/**/*.test.js"`: 641 passing, 74 failing, in suites that already fail on this machine (pixel measurements and timeouts). The number of `MultiEditorTabsControl` timeouts varies from run to run.

Manual test in a Code OSS window, on the first commit of this PR, using temporary commands (not part of this PR) that captured and applied the state, with an editor, a terminal and both side bars open:

- After hiding the side bars and moving the panel, applying the captured arrangement restored the positions and sizes exactly. The editor and the terminal kept their content, and no new errors were logged.
- Applying an arrangement with a hidden panel on the right, while the terminal at the bottom had the focus, hid the panel, and it stayed hidden.
- A maximized secondary side bar and a maximized panel on the right were applied, and restored to their sizes.

Manual test of the changes to the chat part, in a Code OSS window 1340 wide, on c22688935e9 and 5a8e24d23de, with `chat.viewSessions.openChatIn: "chatArea"` and the panel at the bottom. As the chat part blocks maximizing from the UI, `workbench.secondarySideBar.forceMaximized` maximized the secondary side bar. Each came back at the widths from before, with the chat part: side bar 300, chat part 398, editor area 286, secondary side bar 292.

- Maximizing and restoring the secondary side bar beside the chat part, and without it.
- Maximizing it beside the chat part, reloading while maximized, and restoring it. Before the fix above, the side bar came back at 170 and the editor area at 416. With the original order, it came back as before too.
- Hiding the editor area for the chat part, reloading, and showing the editor area again.

Manual test of applying, in a Code OSS window 1340 wide, on f7cfcccc718, with temporary commands (not part of this PR) that captured and applied the state, and the chat in the panel:

- In Zen mode, an applied state shows and hides the parts, and Zen mode stays active. Exiting Zen mode shows the parts that were visible before it started again, in addition to the applied ones.
- A state with the side bar at 400 and the panel on the right at 420 kept its sizes after Reload Window.
- No errors from applying in the renderer log.

Not covered yet:

- Zen mode: exiting it shows the parts that were visible before it started again, also those that a state applied meanwhile hid. The named layouts PR will handle it.
- With the chat part, applying a state is covered by the unit tests only, not by a manual test.
- Applying a state detaches every part from the DOM and attaches it again, which reloads iframes. Webviews that the chat shows inline, such as a Mermaid diagram or tool output, then stay blank until the chat hides and shows again: the chat list reinitializes them when it renders their row again or becomes visible, not when the row reconnects. #350214 fixes it in the chat list.
- With the chat part, maximizing the panel and then the secondary side bar, and restoring both, leaves the chat part at its minimum width, also with the normal commands: restoring the secondary side bar shows the chat part beside the panel that is still maximized, and restoring the panel lets the editor area take its width from the chat part. That is how it already works on `main`, and this PR doesn't change it.
- With the chat part holding the editor area, a maximized secondary side bar that is applied, once restored, doesn't give the editor area back its width when the chat part gives the editor area back, as after a reload in that state on `main`. With the toggles alone, restoring the secondary side bar brings a bottom panel back at its minimum height on `main`. A follow-up PR will fix both where they come from, in maximizing the secondary side bar and in creating the grid for it.
- Showing a part by a user action, such as toggling the side bar, opens its view container without the check above, so an open that waits for the extensions to register can still show that part after it hid again. That is how it already works on `main`, and this PR doesn't change it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or reload the workbench, including maximized panels and secondary side bars
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Grid construction and initial layout remain synchronous. Restoring panes waits for default-view restoration, then restores up to three locations concurrently. Missing containers await the existing shared extension-registration barrier. Startup telemetry is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and enqueue the startupLayout telemetry event to the shared-process appender when telemetry is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed-size event per window startup, before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: createGridDescriptor emitted the same event once. The diff moves that emission to createWorkbenchLayout without increasing its frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local event preparation remains on startup; remote delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold extension-contributed views can activate their extensions and request tree data across the extension-host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three restored pane locations, with up to three sequential container attempts per location. Downstream activation scales with newly activated visible extension views; tree requests retain existing batching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same locations, fallback order, pane-opening service, and extension-view activation paths ran before the diff. Existing callers do not supply the new canOpen callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pane restoration can await extension registration; extension view population proceeds through its existing asynchronous activation/provider paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed eight workbench parts, optionally nine with chat; up to three restored pane locations, containing a user-dependent number of views.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grid creation is serialized on the UI thread. The three restoration branches can overlap, while fallback attempts within each branch are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Layout sizes are already in the state model. Chat-layout reads use the storage service's in-memory cache. Composites are reused by ID, and custom tree activation has an activated guard. Extension readiness uses one shared barrier, not a scan per request. Failed container attempts remain bounded to three per location.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff, restore call sites, shared registration barrier, composite cache, and telemetry client establish unchanged boundary multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup duration depends on extensions and restored content; no timing measurements were collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The grid factory is extracted without an extra startup construction, telemetry remains once per startup, and changed width calculations are bounded arithmetic.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maximize and restore the secondary side bar beside a visible chat part
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visibility changes and grid resizing run synchronously. The changed order preserves chat's own width, and restoration performs at most two additional width corrections, only for visible parts whose widths differ. Terminal backend updates are asynchronous and not awaited by this command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Propagate surviving terminal dimension changes to a local or remote PTY.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per affected terminal and distinct dimensions surviving existing coalescing. Large-buffer horizontal changes are debounced for 100 ms; small buffers resize immediately; unchanged dimensions are rejected by PTY wrappers. The diff adds at most two grid correction passes, not an input-sized loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Maximizing/restoring already changed part visibility and dimensions through the same terminal resize path. Geometry order changes, but this PR does not introduce terminal creation or remove resize coalescing/dimension deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Grid and terminal geometry work occurs on the UI thread; PTY channel completion is off the command's synchronous critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed set of workbench parts and the terminals/content affected by their dimension changes. The new widthsBefore collection has at most two entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Layout mutations are synchronous and serial. Terminal horizontal work is coalesced per terminal for large buffers; backend communication can overlap across terminals.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hidden part widths come from grid cached-visible sizes. The second hide/restore-chat helper call is guarded and does not repeat the visibility transition. Existing composite instances and terminal resize machinery are reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded correction count, helper guards, cached sizes, and the terminal resize path. No independently demonstrated harmful performance mechanism was found in the changed ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of a relayout depends on visible content and terminal count; the extra bounded correction passes have not been profiled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Additional resizes are guarded corrections required to restore widths, and the diff does not establish an unbounded or newly uncoalesced expensive-boundary burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save layout state and reload while chat occupies the editor area
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Saving reads grid sizes, subtracts the cached editor width when necessary, serializes one small chat-layout object, and updates storage. Persistence is batched asynchronously, except that normal shutdown waits for its existing flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed-size record per existing save event, unchanged from before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same save callback serialized the same fixed-size record; the diff changes width arithmetic and hiddenByLayout's value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A bounded serialization occurs synchronously during save.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist changed storage entries through a batched updateItems request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one pending entry for the chat-layout key; equal values are discarded and successive updates to the same key coalesce into the pending map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage key was written on the same save events through the same deduplication and flush path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ordinary writes schedule a delayed flush rather than awaiting disk or IPC from saveChatPartLayout. Existing shutdown flush semantics remain unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One chat-layout object and a fixed number of part-size reads per save, independent of transcript length and editor count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local arithmetic and serialization are serial. Existing storage flush scheduling batches persistence; no new parallel I/O is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both visible dimensions and cached hidden dimensions come from the grid model, not DOM measurement or database reads. Storage uses cached values, equality suppression, and per-key pending-write coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: save registration, fixed record shape, grid accessors, storage equality checks, pending maps, and IPC serialization were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Database latency varies by environment, but the diff does not increase save-event or write cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed work is constant-time cached-size arithmetic, not additional persistence or content-sized serialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Capture and apply a complete parts arrangement using the new API
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository searches found only test callers of the new public methods. If called, applyPartsLayoutState synchronously rebuilds the fixed-size grid, reconnects part elements, lays out, and restores focus. Opening missing panes is launched asynchronously, not awaited by apply.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save the current chat-layout record before rebuilding, when a chat part exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fixed-size chat-layout store per apply, with equality suppression and per-key batched persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The bulk-apply API did not exist. Current production workflows still do not call it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local record creation is synchronous; storage delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Opening a missing visible pane may initialize extension views and use existing extension-host activation/provider channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three pane locations per apply, each with sequential bounded fallback. Already-active panes are skipped; canceled or hidden pending opens are checked before opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no bulk-apply operation. Individual visibility commands already used the underlying pane-opening and activation paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration-dependent pane opening is off apply's synchronous return path, though first usable pane content can depend on it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eight or nine top-level parts, at most three pane opens, and the content held by reconnected part elements. There is no production apply-event frequency in this revision.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grid replacement is synchronous. Up to three pane-opening tasks overlap; fallback attempts within a task are sequential. A later apply invalidates pending opens before their expensive opening step.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parts and composites are reused rather than reconstructed as application objects. The previous grid is disposed, including subscriptions and its DOM element. A MutableDisposable cancels prior apply-open tokens on replacement/disposal. Extension readiness is shared, and active-pane checks suppress redundant opens.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for absence of production callers, fixed top-level cardinality, old-grid cleanup, cancellation checks, and asynchronous opening. Performance of future callers cannot be established from this revision.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A future caller could expose reconnection/layout costs, particularly for embedded content, but its trigger frequency and product reachability are not present in this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No currently reachable production regression to report. Whole-grid reconnection and asynchronous lifecycle behavior were inspected, but reporting a user-visible slowdown here would require inventing a caller or workload.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all three changed files and all diff pages against base 7e993177c9d9fd024e5e0a38061b24c813e9ed6e. Traced startup restoration, telemetry, grid cleanup, chat maximize/restore, persistence, terminal resizing, and the new bulk-layout API. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding or qualifying concrete performance-regression fix was established. Static review only; the new arrangement API currently has no production callers.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
